|148|Close-Grip Bench Press                   |"{\"grip\": \"Pronated grip narrower than shoulder width, typically with the index fingers near or just inside the smooth rings of the bar; wrists stacked directly over the forearms to avoid excessive extension under load.\", \"tldr\": {\"focus\": \"Keep the elbows tucked at roughly 30-45 degrees from the torso throughout the entire press, not flared wide as in a standard bench press.\", \"setup\": \"Lie flat on the bench with a shoulder-width or slightly narrower grip (hands roughly 8-12 inches apart, just outside the shoulders), bar over the lower sternum.\", \"execution\": \"Lower the bar to the lower chest with the elbows tracking close to the torso, then press it back up and slightly back toward the shoulders as the elbows extend.\", \"stop_when\": \"The elbows can no longer be kept tucked and begin flaring outward to complete the rep, or the bar path stalls and drifts forward off the intended trajectory.\"}, \"stance\": \"Feet flat on the floor, positioned to allow leg drive without lifting the hips off the bench.\", \"bracing\": \"Maintain scapular retraction against the bench throughout the set; brace the abdomen and keep the ribcage from flaring upward as the bar descends, preventing the torso from arching excessively to shorten the effective range of motion.\", \"overview\": \"This is the flat barbell bench press performed with a narrower-than-standard grip to bias elbow-extensor (triceps) involvement while still recruiting the pectoralis major and anterior deltoid. The defining characteristic distinguishing it from the standard bench press is the reduced grip width combined with a deliberately tucked elbow path, which shifts the forearm toward a more vertical position under the bar and shortens the moment arm at the elbow relative to the shoulder. This variant is distinct from a board press or a floor press in that full range of motion to the chest is used, and distinct from a JM press or triceps-extension-bench-press hybrid in that the bar path remains a standard straight press rather than incorporating an intentional skull-crusher component.\", \"eccentric\": \"Lower the bar under control to the lower sternum/upper abdomen area, allowing the elbows to bend while keeping them tracking close to the ribs rather than drifting out to the sides; the descent path should mirror the ascent path.\", \"concentric\": \"Press the bar upward and slightly back toward the face/shoulders as the elbows extend, keeping the elbows tucked close to the torso rather than flaring laterally; the bar path moves in a slight arc rather than a straight vertical line.\", \"tempo_notes\": \"Controlled descent without bouncing the bar off the chest; a brief pause at the chest is acceptable but not required, and continuous tension should be maintained rather than resting the bar on the sternum.\", \"end_position\": \"Arms fully extended with the bar directly over the shoulders (not over the face or lower chest), elbows locked without hyperextension, scapulae still retracted.\", \"safety_notes\": [\"Use a spotter or safety pins given the reduced leverage and higher joint stress at the elbow with a narrow grip.\", \"Avoid gripping narrower than a hand's width inside shoulder-width, as this can place excessive strain on the wrists and elbows.\", \"Keep the wrists stacked over the forearms rather than allowing them to bend backward under load.\"], \"external_cues\": \"Push the bar up and slightly back toward the rack; keep the elbows pointed at the floor, not out toward the plates.\", \"internal_cues\": \"Drive the elbows straight down and up along the ribs; think of bending and straightening only at the elbow while the upper arm stays close to the torso.\", \"common_mistakes\": [\"Flaring the elbows outward toward a standard bench press angle to recruit more chest and reduce triceps demand.\", \"Gripping too narrow, causing excessive wrist extension and forearm strain.\", \"Bouncing the bar off the chest to gain momentum through the sticking point.\", \"Arching excessively or lifting the hips to shorten the effective range of motion.\", \"Allowing the bar to drift toward the neck or face during the descent instead of the lower sternum.\"], \"equipment_setup\": \"Standard flat bench with a barbell rack set at a height allowing unracking without excessive shoulder elevation; a spotter or safety pins are advisable given the reduced leverage at lockout.\", \"range_of_motion\": \"Full range from bar contact at the lower sternum/upper abdominal region to full elbow extension at lockout; equipment (chest depth) defines the bottom limit rather than an arbitrary stopping point.\", \"rir_0_definition\": \"Inability to complete elbow extension to lockout while keeping the elbows in the tucked path and the hips/shoulders in contact with the bench, distinct from being unable to move the bar at all.\", \"rir_1_indicators\": \"Noticeably slower bar speed off the chest, a slight but still controlled increase in elbow flare, and a longer sticking point near the mid-range while full ROM and elbow position are still preserved.\", \"individualization\": \"Exact grip width may vary moderately based on wrist and shoulder comfort and forearm length, provided the forearms remain close to vertical at the bottom position and the elbows stay tucked rather than flared. Degree of thoracic arch and bar touch point on the torso may vary slightly with torso length and shoulder mobility, as long as the shoulders and hips remain in contact with the bench throughout the rep.\", \"plane_of_movement\": \"Primarily sagittal-plane elbow extension and glenohumeral horizontal adduction/flexion, with a smaller frontal-plane component from scapular retraction on the bench.\", \"starting_position\": \"Shoulder blades retracted and pinned against the bench, mild thoracic extension creating a slight arch, feet flat on the floor, bar unracked and held directly over the lower sternum with arms extended.\", \"technical_failure\": \"The point at which the elbows can no longer be held close to the torso and begin flaring outward to generate additional leverage, or the bar path deviates forward/stalls such that lockout cannot be completed without the hips rising off the bench.\", \"primary_joint_actions\": \"Elbow extension is the dominant joint action, occurring with the forearm closer to vertical than in a standard-grip bench press; glenohumeral flexion/horizontal adduction is reduced in range compared to wide-grip pressing. The scapulae remain retracted and depressed against the bench as a stabilizing platform rather than moving through the rep.\"}" |56 |Deadlift                                 |"{\"grip\": \"Grip the bar just outside the legs with the arms vertical when viewed from the front. A double-overhand, hook, or mixed grip may be used provided both elbows remain fully extended and the bar stays level; with a mixed grip, keep the supinated arm straight and avoid actively curling either side.\", \"tldr\": {\"focus\": \"Keep the bar vertically over the midfoot and close to the body while the hips and shoulders rise together from the floor.\", \"setup\": \"Stand with the midfoot under the bar, feet around hip width, grip just outside the legs, and set the torso by bringing the shins to the bar without rolling it forward.\", \"execution\": \"Brace, push the floor away, and extend the knees and hips while keeping the bar in close contact with the legs until standing tall.\", \"stop_when\": \"Stop when another repetition would require major spinal rounding, a pronounced hip shoot, loss of midfoot balance, hitching, or incomplete hip and knee extension.\"}, \"stance\": \"Use a symmetrical stance generally around hip width with the toes pointing forward or slightly outward according to hip anatomy. Keep the entire foot in contact with the floor and position the knees so they can track naturally without forcing the arms outward.\", \"bracing\": \"Create circumferential abdominal pressure before the bar leaves the floor and maintain the ribcage and pelvis as a rigid unit. Brace the spinal extensors and engage the lats enough to keep the bar close to the legs without trying to row it upward. Avoid lumbar hyperextension at the start or lockout.\", \"overview\": \"A conventional barbell deadlift performed from the floor with the feet inside the hands and the bar traveling anterior to the legs. The active-tension profile supports a hip-dominant conventional pull with substantial posterior-chain demand and a meaningful but smaller knee-extension contribution. The defining mechanics are coordinated hip and knee extension around a bar maintained close to the body and vertically balanced over the midfoot.\", \"eccentric\": \"Begin the descent by hinging the hips backward while keeping the bar close to the thighs. Once the bar passes the knees, allow the knees to flex and continue lowering the bar vertically along the shins until the plates return to the floor. Maintain trunk rigidity and whole-foot balance throughout rather than squatting the bar around the knees or letting it drift forward.\", \"concentric\": \"From the braced floor position, push through the whole foot and extend the knees and hips while maintaining the bar directly over the midfoot. The hips and shoulders should rise together initially, with the bar traveling vertically in close contact with or immediately adjacent to the shins and thighs. As the bar passes the knees, continue extending the hips and knees until standing tall with the bar against the thighs.\", \"tempo_notes\": \"Take tension out of the body-bar system before breaking the plates from the floor rather than jerking the bar upward. Do not bounce the plates between repetitions, deliberately hitch the bar on the thighs, or accelerate the eccentric uncontrollably into the floor.\", \"end_position\": \"Finish standing tall with the hips and knees fully extended, shoulders stacked over the pelvis, arms straight, and the bar resting against the upper thighs. The lockout should come from hip and knee extension rather than leaning backward or hyperextending the lumbar spine.\", \"safety_notes\": [\"Keep both elbows fully extended throughout the pull, especially when using a mixed grip.\", \"Use secure collars when appropriate and ensure the loading is symmetrical.\", \"Maintain a controlled bar path close to the legs without deliberately scraping or striking the shins.\", \"Do not force a floor start from an artificially low bar height that prevents a stable conventional deadlift position.\"], \"external_cues\": \"Push the floor away and drag the bar straight up the legs until you are standing tall.\", \"internal_cues\": \"Brace before pulling; keep the armpits tight and the arms long; extend the hips and knees while maintaining pressure through the whole foot.\", \"common_mistakes\": [\"Starting with the bar too far in front of the midfoot and allowing it to remain separated from the legs during the pull.\", \"Dropping the hips excessively and attempting to squat the bar from the floor.\", \"Allowing the hips to shoot upward before the bar leaves the floor and converting the lift toward a stiff-legged pull.\", \"Rounding the lumbar or thoracic spine substantially as force is applied from the floor.\", \"Pulling the bar around the knees instead of maintaining a near-vertical path.\", \"Flexing the elbows or attempting to curl the bar during the pull.\", \"Hitching the bar on the thighs or repeatedly re-bending the knees to complete lockout.\", \"Finishing by leaning backward and hyperextending the lumbar spine.\"], \"equipment_setup\": \"Use a standard barbell loaded symmetrically with full-diameter plates or an equivalent setup that establishes conventional deadlift height from the floor. Position the bar on a level surface where it can travel vertically without obstruction.\", \"range_of_motion\": \"Lift from the standardized floor position to full standing hip and knee extension, then return the plates to the floor. The starting joint angles may vary with limb proportions, but the bar should remain over the midfoot and the lifter should not artificially lower the hips into a squat or elevate them into a stiff-legged starting position that disrupts the intended conventional geometry.\", \"rir_0_definition\": \"RIR 0 is reached when no additional repetition can be completed from the floor to full lockout within the defined conventional deadlift standard, even if the bar could still be moved by major spinal rounding, allowing the hips to shoot upward, hitching the bar on the thighs, shifting balance forward, or shortening the range.\", \"rir_1_indicators\": \"Approximately one technically valid repetition may remain when bar speed slows substantially from the floor or around knee height and effort is visibly high, but the lifter can still maintain spinal position, a close vertical bar path, whole-foot balance, coordinated hip and knee extension, and a complete lockout with only minor technical drift.\", \"individualization\": \"Stance width, toe angle, grip width, hip height, knee flexion, torso inclination, and exact shoulder position relative to the bar vary with femur length, tibial length, torso length, arm length, and hip anatomy. These differences are legitimate provided the bar begins over the midfoot, the arms hang outside the legs, the spine remains controlled, and the bar follows a close vertical path. Grip style may also vary; double-overhand, hook, and mixed grips all preserve the exercise identity if the arms remain straight and the bar stays symmetrical.\", \"plane_of_movement\": \"Primarily sagittal-plane hip and knee flexion-extension, with the spine maintained substantially isometric and the pelvis, knees, shoulders, and trunk stabilized against frontal- and transverse-plane deviation.\", \"starting_position\": \"Stand with the bar over the midfoot, typically a few centimeters from the shins, and the feet around hip width. Hinge down and grip the bar just outside the legs, then bring the shins to the bar without pushing it forward. Set the hips at the height created by this geometry, keep the shoulders slightly in front of or approximately over the bar depending on proportions, maintain a stable neutral-to-individually consistent spinal position, and create tension through the trunk and upper back before initiating the pull.\", \"technical_failure\": \"Technical failure occurs when another repetition cannot be completed from the floor to full standing without a material breakdown such as substantial lumbar or thoracic flexion, the hips shooting upward before the bar breaks the floor, the bar drifting materially away from the legs, loss of midfoot balance, marked knee valgus, asymmetric bar elevation, elbow flexion, thigh hitching, repeated re-bending of the knees to finish, or failure to achieve controlled hip and knee extension.\", \"primary_joint_actions\": \"Concentric hip extension and knee extension with ankle plantarflexor stabilization. The lumbar and thoracic spine remain substantially isometric, while the shoulder girdle, elbows, wrists, and hands stabilize the bar; the glenohumeral joints remain relatively fixed with the arms hanging vertically.\"}"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|124|Smith Machine Romanian Deadlift          |"{\"grip\": \"Pronated grip just outside the thighs, wide enough that the bar can pass close to the legs without hitting the knees; wrists remain neutral, not flexed or extended under load.\", \"tldr\": {\"focus\": \"Push the hips straight back as the torso lowers, keeping the bar traveling in a straight vertical line against the legs.\", \"setup\": \"Bar racked at hip-crease height on the Smith machine, feet hip-width apart and close to the bar's fixed vertical path.\", \"execution\": \"Hinge at the hips to lower the bar along its fixed track down the front of the thighs while keeping the knees only slightly bent, then drive the hips forward to return to standing.\", \"stop_when\": \"The lumbar spine begins to round or the hips can no longer be driven forward without the knees bending significantly to compensate.\"}, \"stance\": \"Feet approximately hip-width apart, positioned so the bar's fixed vertical path travels directly over the mid-foot to lace of the shoe throughout the hinge.\", \"bracing\": \"Brace the abdominal wall to keep the ribcage stacked over the pelvis and maintain lumbar neutrality throughout the hinge; the erector spinae work isometrically to resist further lumbar flexion as the torso inclines forward.\", \"overview\": \"This is a hip-hinge posterior-chain exercise performed on a Smith machine, using the machine's fixed vertical bar path instead of a free-weight bar. The Romanian deadlift variant is distinguished from a conventional or stiff-leg deadlift by starting from a standing position (not the floor) with minimal knee flexion, emphasizing hip flexion/extension under a lengthened hamstring-gluteal position. The Smith machine's fixed track removes the need to balance the bar path anteroposteriorly, allowing the lifter to focus purely on hip hinge mechanics without horizontal bar drift.\", \"eccentric\": \"Initiate by pushing the hips backward while allowing the torso to incline forward, keeping the knees at a nearly constant slight bend; the bar rises in a straight vertical line as the hips complete extension.\", \"tempo_notes\": \"Lower under continuous control without allowing the fixed carriage to free-fall; a brief pause at end-range depth can help confirm position, but bouncing off end-range tension should be avoided since the machine offers no elastic bar give.\", \"end_position\": \"Standing tall with hips fully extended, glutes contracted, torso vertical, and the bar returned to the thigh/hip-crease starting height.\", \"safety_notes\": [\"Confirm the Smith machine carriage hooks or safety catches are set at an appropriate height before unracking, in case the bar needs to be re-racked mid-set.\", \"Avoid excessive forward hip travel beyond the point where lumbar neutrality can be held, since the fixed bar path will not correct for a rounding spine the way a free bar's path might.\"], \"external_cues\": \"Keep the bar brushing lightly against the thighs and shins on the way down; taller lifters or those with longer torsos relative to femur length may reach technical failure at a shallower hinge angle. Knee flexion angle at the start may be set slightly higher or lower depending on comfort, provided it remains essentially constant throughout the repetition rather than increasing at depth.\", \"plane_of_movement\": \"Primarily sagittal-plane hip flexion and extension, with the bar constrained to a purely vertical path by the machine track; the torso inclines forward and returns to upright with minimal frontal- or transverse-plane movement.\", \"starting_position\": \"Stand with the bar resting against the upper thighs/hip crease, knees slightly bent and fixed in that flexion angle, torso upright, shoulder blades retracted, and a slight forward lean already present at the hips.\", \"technical_failure\": \"The point at which the lumbar spine begins to flex (rounding) to permit further hip flexion, or the knees bend substantially to substitute for hip extension during the ascent, altering the hinge into a squat-like pattern.\", \"primary_joint_actions\": \"Hip flexion during the descent and hip extension during the ascent, with the knees maintaining a small, largely fixed degree of flexion throughout; the lumbar spine and thoracic spine are stabilized in a neutral position rather than actively flexing or extending; the shoulders and elbows remain fixed to transmit bar load to the hands.\"}" |178|Spider Curl                              |"{\"grip\": \"Neutral or semi-supinated grip on the dumbbells, palms facing each other or rotating slightly toward supination as the elbows flex; wrists held stable and not allowed to flex or extend excessively to assist the curl.\", \"tldr\": {\"focus\": \"Keep the upper arms motionless against the pad throughout the repetition so only the elbow joint moves.\", \"setup\": \"Set the incline bench to a steep angle and drape the torso over the top pad so the chest and upper abdomen are firmly supported, with both arms hanging straight down holding dumbbells.\", \"execution\": \"Flex both elbows to curl the dumbbells upward while the upper arms stay vertical and pinned against the pad, then lower under control back to full elbow extension.\", \"stop_when\": \"The chest begins to lift off the pad or the upper arms swing backward to help complete the curl.\"}, \"stance\": \"Feet planted on the floor or a raised platform behind the bench, providing a stable base while the torso leans forward into the pad.\", \"bracing\": \"Chest and upper abdomen pressed firmly and continuously into the pad to prevent the torso from lifting or the shoulders from extending backward to assist the lift; core engaged to prevent trunk sway.\", \"overview\": \"This is the chest-supported spider curl performed bilaterally over the top of a steep incline bench, distinct from the incline dumbbell curl performed lying back against the pad. |122|Barbell Romanian Deadlift                |"{\"grip\": \"Pronated, double-overhand or mixed grip, hands just outside the thighs so the arms hang vertically and the bar can track along the legs without the hands contacting the hips.\", \"tldr\": {\"focus\": \"Push the hips backward first and keep the bar in contact with the legs throughout the descent.\", \"setup\": \"Stand with a pronated grip just outside the thighs, barbell against the front of the legs, knees softly flexed and fixed for the set.\", \"execution\": \"Hinge the hips backward to lower the bar along the thighs while the spine stays neutral and knee angle barely changes, then drive the hips forward to return to standing.\", \"stop_when\": \"The lumbar spine begins to round or the bar drifts forward off the thighs to maintain hip drive.\"}, \"stance\": \"Feet approximately hip-width, toes forward or very slightly turned out, weight distributed through the mid-foot and heel throughout the movement.\", \"bracing\": \"Brace the abdominal wall and maintain rib-to-pelvis alignment before initiating the hinge; the erector spinae contract isometrically to resist lumbar flexion as the trunk tips forward, and the lats engage to keep the bar pulled tight against the legs.\", \"overview\": \"The barbell Romanian deadlift is a hip-hinge exercise performed from a standing start with the bar already in hand, distinguishing it from the conventional deadlift, which begins from the floor with greater knee flexion and a different pulling pattern. |132|Pendulum Squat                           |"{\"grip\": \"\", \"tldr\": {\"focus\": \"Let the knees travel forward over the toes and keep the shins tracking in line with the feet as the arm arcs.\", \"setup\": \"Stand on the footplate with your back and shoulders pressed against the pendulum's pads, feet set slightly forward of the pivot point, hip- to shoulder-width apart.\", \"execution\": \"Bend the knees and hips to let the pendulum arm arc downward and backward, then drive through the feet to reverse the arc and return to the top.\", \"stop_when\": \"You can no longer keep the heels planted and the torso pinned against the back pad through the full arc without the knees caving or the hips shooting back.\"}, \"stance\": \"Feet approximately hip- to shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly; foot placement on the platform (higher vs. lower, narrower vs. wider) determines how far forward the knees travel and how deep the achievable arc becomes.\", \"bracing\": \"Press the upper back and shoulders firmly into the pads throughout the set so the torso does not shift or round; maintain a neutral pelvis and avoid allowing the low back to round away from the pad as the pendulum reaches its lowest point.\", \"overview\": \"The plate-loaded pendulum squat is a machine-based, fixed-arc squat pattern in which the resistance is applied through a pivoting lever (the pendulum) rather than a straight vertical or guided linear track. |162|T-Bar Row                                |"{\"grip\": \"Neutral, close grip on the V-handle attachment with palms facing each other; hands remain close together throughout the movement, which favors greater elbow-flexor involvement than a wide pronated bar grip.\", \"tldr\": {\"focus\": \"Drive the elbows back and slightly outward past the ribcage rather than simply flexing the arms.\", \"setup\": \"Load one end of a barbell into a landmine attachment, straddle the sleeve, and hinge forward at the hips to roughly 30-45° from the floor with a flat spine.\", \"execution\": \"Pull the handle up and back toward the lower ribs/upper abdomen by driving the elbows behind the torso, then lower under control to full arm extension without losing the hip hinge.\", \"stop_when\": \"The torso begins to swing upright using hip extension to help move the handle, or the lower back rounds to complete the pull.\"}, \"stance\": \"Feet straddle the barbell sleeve, positioned wide enough for the bar to travel unobstructed through its arc; stance width may vary but should allow the hips to stay stacked over mid-foot without shifting during the pull.\", \"bracing\": \"Maintain a braced abdominal wall and neutral spine to resist lumbar flexion under load; the hip hinge angle is held constant by isometric erector spinae and glute activity rather than being re-established each repetition.\", \"overview\": \"This is the standing, bent-over landmine T-bar row performed with a close, neutral-grip handle attached at the loaded end of the barbell. The lifter straddles the bar and maintains a fixed forward-leaning hip hinge throughout the set, pulling the handle to the torso along an arcing path dictated by the landmine pivot. Compared to the chest-supported T-bar row, this variant requires continuous isometric control of the hip hinge and lumbar spine, which increases erector spinae and abdominal wall demand alongside the pulling musculature.\", \"eccentric\": \"Lower the handle back down along the same arc by allowing the shoulders to protract slightly and the elbows to extend, returning to full arm extension while the hip hinge angle and spinal position remain unchanged.\", \"concentric\": \"Pull the handle upward and backward along the arc created by the landmine pivot, initiating by drawing the shoulder blades together and driving the elbows past the torso toward the hips; the torso and hip angle remain fixed while the handle travels toward the lower ribcage or upper abdomen.\", \"tempo_notes\": \"Avoid using a downward torso bounce or hip drive to initiate the pull; the bar should move continuously without a jerking motion at the bottom of each repetition.\", \"end_position\": \"The handle reaches the lower ribs or upper abdomen with the elbows drawn behind the plane of the torso and the scapulae fully retracted, without the torso rising toward vertical.\", \"safety_notes\": [\"Ensure the landmine sleeve or floor anchor is secure before loading to prevent the bar from shifting laterally during the pull.\", \"Maintain a neutral cervical spine; avoid craning the neck upward to look forward during the hinge.\"], \"external_cues\": \"Pull the handle toward your belt line; keep the torso angle fixed relative to the floor as the bar travels.\", \"internal_cues\": \"Draw the elbows back past the ribs; attach a close-grip V-handle or similar neutral-grip attachment to the loaded end near the collar.\", \"range_of_motion\": \"From full elbow extension and scapular protraction at the bottom to full scapular retraction with elbows behind the torso at the top; Stance width and knee bend can be adjusted to accommodate hip mobility and bar clearance without altering the pulling mechanics.\", \"plane_of_movement\": \"Primarily sagittal-plane shoulder extension and elbow flexion, combined with scapular retraction in the scapular plane; the torso remains in a fixed sagittal-plane hip-hinge position that does not move independently during the repetition.\", \"starting_position\": \"Stand straddling the barbell with feet roughly shoulder-width apart, knees softly bent, hips hinged so the torso sits at approximately 30-45° above horizontal, spine in a neutral (flat, not rounded or hyperextended) position, arms hanging directly below the shoulders holding the handle with elbows extended.\", \"technical_failure\": \"The set reaches technical failure when the lifter can no longer draw the handle to the torso without extending the hips to add momentum, rounding the lumbar spine, or allowing the torso to rise noticeably toward vertical during the pull.\", \"primary_joint_actions\": \"Glenohumeral extension and horizontal extension driving the upper arm back relative to the torso; elbow flexion as the forearm curls toward the ribs; scapular retraction and slight downward rotation; hip and lumbar spine are held isometrically in a flexed-forward position rather than actively moving.\"}" |188|Kneeling Machine Hip Thrust              |"{\"grip\": \"Hands typically rest on the side handles or frame solely for balance; grip does not contribute to force production and should not be used to assist the hip drive.\", \"tldr\": {\"focus\": \"Initiate the movement by contracting the glutes to extend the hips, not by arching the lower back.\", \"setup\": \"Kneel on the padded platform with knees fixed under the hips, upper back braced against the support pad, and the hip pad positioned low across the pelvis just below the belt line.\", \"execution\": \"Drive the hips forward into extension against the pad, keeping the knees fixed in place and the torso locked against the back support throughout.\", \"stop_when\": \"You can no longer achieve full hip extension without the lumbar spine hyperextending or the torso lifting off the back pad.\"}, \"stance\": \"Knee width approximately hip-width, with knees and lower legs remaining stationary on the platform for the entire set.\", \"bracing\": \"Maintain a neutral lumbar spine by keeping the ribcage aligned over the pelvis and lightly bracing the abdominal wall; the upper back should stay in constant contact with the support pad so that force is transmitted through hip extension rather than through lumbar arching.\", \"overview\": \"This is a plate-loaded machine hip thrust performed from a kneeling position, with the knees fixed on a padded platform, the upper back locked against a support pad, and resistance applied through a hip pad positioned across the anterior pelvis. Unlike the barbell or bodyweight hip thrust performed supine with feet on the floor, this variant fixes the knee angle mechanically and isolates hip extension through a lever arm, removing ankle and knee contribution to the movement. The kneeling geometry places the hip joint into a deep flexed starting position, producing a long hip-extension arc dominated by the gluteus maximus with substantial hamstring and adductor magnus synergy.\", \"eccentric\": \"Allow the hip pad to return along the same arc as the hips flex back toward the starting position, controlling the descent so the pelvis does not drop suddenly under the load. The torso remains against the back pad and the knees stay fixed throughout the return.\", \"concentric\": \"Drive the pelvis forward by extending the hips, pushing the hip pad through its arc until the hips reach full extension. The knees remain fixed on the platform and do not extend or shift position; the torso stays anchored against the back pad without pushing into additional extension. Force should be felt originating from the glutes and posterior thigh rather than from the lower back.\", \"tempo_notes\": \"Avoid bouncing the hip pad off the bottom stop between repetitions; maintain continuous tension through the glutes across the full arc rather than resting at the bottom.\", \"end_position\": \"Hips fully extended, glutes maximally contracted, torso still supported against the back pad, and no lumbar hyperextension present.\", \"safety_notes\": [\"Ensure the hip pad is positioned below the anterior superior iliac spines rather than directly on the abdomen to avoid discomfort or restricted breathing.\", \"Confirm the knee platform padding adequately supports the knees given the sustained kneeling load throughout the set.\", \"Avoid forcing additional range through lumbar hyperextension once hip extension is complete.\"], \"external_cues\": \"Push the hip pad forward and up through its arc; keep the upper back pinned to the support pad throughout the movement.\", \"internal_cues\": \"Squeeze the glutes to drive the hips forward; keep the ribcage stacked over the pelvis rather than letting the lower back arch.\", \"common_mistakes\": [\"Arching the lower back to complete the final portion of hip extension instead of driving through the glutes.\", \"Allowing the torso to lift off the back pad as the load increases.\", \"Letting the knees shift forward or backward on the platform during the set.\", \"Bouncing out of the bottom position rather than controlling the transition from flexion to extension.\", \"Stopping short of full hip extension while still moving the pad, resulting in a truncated range.\"], \"equipment_setup\": \"Adjust the knee platform and hip pad so that, in the bottom position, the hips are flexed to roughly 90 degrees or slightly beyond, and the hip pad contacts the pelvis below the anterior superior iliac spines rather than on the abdomen. Set the upper-back pad height so the torso remains supported without requiring active trunk extension to stay in contact.\", \"range_of_motion\": \"From a deeply flexed hip position defined by the kneeling geometry to full hip extension permitted by the machine's lever arm; the endpoint is defined by the point at which further hip extension would require lumbar extension rather than additional hip motion.\", \"rir_0_definition\": \"Inability to complete hip extension through the full intended range while keeping the torso against the back pad and the lumbar spine neutral, regardless of whether the pad can still be moved through a partial or compensated range.\", \"rir_1_indicators\": \"Noticeably slower hip drive through the middle of the range, increased effort to reach full hip extension, but the torso remains against the pad and the lumbar spine stays neutral.\", \"individualization\": \"Hip pad height and knee platform position may be adjusted moderately for femur length and hip anatomy, provided the starting hip flexion angle remains deep enough to produce a meaningful extension arc and the knees stay fixed throughout. Torso angle against the back pad may vary slightly with limb proportions as long as constant contact is maintained and no active lumbar extension is required to sustain it.\", \"plane_of_movement\": \"Primarily sagittal-plane hip extension and flexion, with the knee and torso held in fixed positions by the machine structure.\", \"starting_position\": \"Kneeling with knees directly beneath the hips, shins resting on the platform, upper back flush against the support pad, hips flexed so the pelvis is tilted posteriorly and the hip pad is loaded against the front of the pelvis. The spine is held in a neutral, not rounded, position.\", \"technical_failure\": \"The point at which full hip extension can no longer be achieved without the torso lifting off the back pad, the lumbar spine hyperextending to complete the range, or the knees shifting position on the platform to assist the movement.\", \"primary_joint_actions\": \"Hip extension from a flexed position toward a neutral or slightly extended hip, produced by the gluteus maximus, hamstrings, and adductor magnus. The knee joint remains in a fixed flexed position throughout, acting as a stable pivot rather than a moving joint. The lumbar spine and thoracic spine are stabilized in a neutral position against the upper-back pad rather than contributing active flexion or extension.\"}" |114|Horizontal Cable Woodchopper             |"{\"grip\": \"Both hands on the handle in a neutral or slightly overlapping grip, arms extended but elbows not locked out.\", \"tldr\": {\"focus\": \"Drive the rotation from the thoracic spine and ribcage, using the arms only as a rigid link to the handle.\", \"setup\": \"Set the cable pulley at chest/sternum height and stand perpendicular to the cable path with arms extended holding the handle.\", \"execution\": \"Rotate the trunk away from the stack to sweep the handle horizontally across the body, then control the return without letting the cable yank you back.\", \"stop_when\": \"The handle path stops staying horizontal or you begin generating rotation from the arms/lumbar spine instead of the trunk.\"}, \"stance\": \"Athletic shoulder-width stance oriented perpendicular to the cable line; a slight pivot of the trailing foot is permitted to assist rotation.\", \"bracing\": \"Brace the abdominal wall to control rotation through the thoracic spine and ribcage while keeping the pelvis relatively stable, avoiding compensatory lumbar hyperextension or excessive hip drive.\", \"overview\": \"This is the standing, chest-height variant of the cable woodchopper, performed with the pulley set level with the sternum so the handle travels in a single horizontal arc rather than the diagonal high-to-low or low-to-high path used in other chop variants. This distinguishes it from diagonal woodchoppers, which combine rotation with a vertical component and load the obliques together with hip- and shoulder-girdle musculature in a different ratio.\", and controlled return are still maintained.\", \"individualization\": \"Stance width and the amount of foot/hip pivot used to assist rotation may vary with hip and thoracic mobility, provided the |154|Pronated Lat Pulldown                    |"{\"grip\": \"Pronated grip with hands set approximately at shoulder width, forearms oriented close to vertical at the top position; wrists remain neutral rather than flexed or extended under load.\", \"tldr\": {\"focus\": \"Initiate the pull by depressing and retracting the scapulae before the elbows flex further, rather than yanking with the arms first.\", \"setup\": \"Seated with thighs secured under the pad, gripping the bar pronated at approximately shoulder width, arms fully extended overhead.\", \"execution\": \"Pull the bar down toward the upper chest by driving the elbows down and back, keeping the torso nearly upright with only a slight backward lean.\", \"stop_when\": \"You can no longer draw the bar to the upper chest without throwing the torso backward or shrugging the shoulders upward.\"}, \"stance\": \"Seated with feet flat on the floor for a stable base; knees fixed by the thigh pad.\", \"bracing\": \"Maintain a neutral spine with the ribcage stacked over the pelvis; brace the trunk lightly to prevent the lower back from arching excessively as the bar descends.\", \"overview\": \"This is a seated cable lat pulldown performed with a pronated, shoulder-width grip, distinguishing it from wide-grip variants by placing the forearms closer to vertical and the hands roughly in line with the shoulders. The narrower pronated grip increases elbow-flexor involvement (biceps brachii, brachialis) relative to a wide-grip pulldown while still emphasizing latissimus dorsi as the primary mover. The torso remains close to vertical with only a slight controlled lean at the bottom of the pull, distinguishing it from a more exaggerated lean-back pulldown style.\", \"eccentric\": \"Allow the bar to rise under control along the same path it descended, returning the torso to upright as the arms extend and the scapulae progressively elevate and protract, finishing with full elbow extension overhead.\", \"concentric\": \"Pull the bar downward and slightly toward the body by driving the elbows down and back along the sides of the ribcage, allowing a small controlled backward lean of the torso (roughly 10-20 degrees) as the bar approaches the upper chest; the scapulae depress and retract as the arms move.\", \"tempo_notes\": \"Maintain continuous tension throughout; avoid using upward momentum from the hips or a rapid backward torso jerk to initiate the pull.\", \"end_position\": \"Bar at approximately upper chest / clavicle level with elbows pointing down and slightly back, torso in a mild backward lean, scapulae fully retracted and depressed.\", \"safety_notes\": [\"Ensure the thigh pad is snug before beginning the set to prevent the body being pulled upward off the seat by the cable.\", \"Avoid pulling the bar behind the cervical spine, which places the neck and shoulder in a vulnerable position.\", \"Control the ascent of the bar to prevent the shoulders from being jerked into abrupt overhead extension at the top.\"], \"external_cues\": \"Pull the bar to the top of the chest; drive the elbows toward the back pockets.\", \"internal_cues\": \"Draw the elbows down toward the hips before the hands finish the pull; feel the shoulder blades slide down and together at the bottom.\", \"common_mistakes\": [\"Initiating the pull with elbow flexion (arms) before scapular depression and retraction occur.\", \"Leaning back excessively and using torso extension to substitute for shoulder and scapular motion.\", \"Shrugging the shoulders upward as the bar descends instead of keeping the traps relaxed until scapular depression is required.\", \"Pulling the bar behind the neck or too low toward the abdomen rather than to the upper chest.\", \"Allowing the wrists to flex under load instead of maintaining a neutral wrist position.\", \"Using rapid, bouncing repetitions that rely on momentum from the top overhead position.\"], \"equipment_setup\": \"Adjust the thigh pad so it firmly contacts the tops of the thighs when seated, preventing the body from lifting off the seat during the pull; the cable attachment is a straight bar positioned at the top of the tower.\", \"range_of_motion\": \"From full overhead elbow extension with scapulae elevated to the bar reaching the upper chest with elbows below the torso; ROM is limited by the point at which further pulling requires torso swing rather than additional shoulder and scapular motion.\", \"rir_0_definition\": \"The bar cannot be pulled to the upper chest without a marked increase in torso lean, a forward head-and-neck jut, or an upward shrug substituting for scapular depression and elbow drive.\", \"rir_1_indicators\": \"The bar's descent visibly slows and requires a longer pause before the scapulae fully engage; the backward lean becomes slightly more pronounced but the bar still reaches the upper chest with the same elbow path.\", \"individualization\": \"Grip width may vary slightly around shoulder width depending on shoulder width and wrist comfort, provided the forearms remain close to vertical at the top of the movement. The degree of backward torso lean at the bottom of the pull may vary modestly with torso length and hip mobility, but should remain a controlled, fixed amount rather than increasing repetition to repetition.\", \"plane_of_movement\": \"Primarily sagittal-plane glenohumeral extension/adduction with a smaller frontal-plane adduction component due to the narrower grip; scapular motion occurs mainly in the frontal plane (depression/retraction).\", \"starting_position\": \"Seated with hips and knees at roughly 90 degrees, feet flat on the floor, thighs locked under the pad, spine in a neutral upright posture, arms fully extended overhead gripping the bar.\", \"technical_failure\": \"Failure occurs when the bar can only be brought to the chest by exaggerating the backward torso lean beyond the initial controlled range, by shrugging the shoulders upward at the start of the pull, or by using a rebounding upward jerk of the arms from the top position.\", \"primary_joint_actions\": \"Glenohumeral extension and adduction combined with elbow flexion; scapulae move from an elevated, protracted position at the top toward depression and retraction at the bottom; the trunk and hips |157|Single-Arm Lat Pulldown                  |"{\"grip\": \"Neutral (palm facing inward) grip on the D-handle; wrist held in a neutral, non-flexed position throughout.\", \"tldr\": {\"focus\": \"Initiate the pull by driving the elbow down toward the hip rather than by flexing the elbow first.\", \"setup\": \"Sit facing a high pulley fitted with a single D-handle, thighs secured under a pad, torso upright and slightly reclined from vertical.\", \"execution\": \"Pull the handle down and back toward the lower ribs/hip on the working side by driving the elbow down and behind the torso, while the opposite hand rests on the thigh or knee for support.\", \"stop_when\": \"You can no longer pull the handle to the lower ribcage without rotating the trunk toward the working arm or leaning backward to substitute momentum for lat contraction.\"}, \"stance\": \"Seated, both feet flat on the floor, thighs secured under the pad; no lower-body movement contributes to the pull.\", \"bracing\": \"Brace the abdominal wall and obliques on the non-working side to resist trunk rotation toward the working arm; keep the pelvis square to the pulley and avoid using the free hand to pull the body sideways for extra range.\", \"overview\": \"This is a unilateral cable lat pulldown performed with a neutral-grip (vertical) D-handle attached to a high pulley, executed one arm at a time while seated with the thighs anchored. Because only one side is loaded, the exercise carries an inherent anti-rotation and anti-lateral-flexion demand on the trunk that bilateral pulldowns do not require. The neutral grip keeps the forearm in a mid-pronation position, reducing biceps-supination demand compared with a supinated single-arm pulldown and shifting more of the pulling emphasis onto the latissimus dorsi and teres major with the elbow tracking close to the torso.\", \"eccentric\": \"Allow the handle to return along the same path under control, extending the shoulder back overhead as the scapula elevates and protracts, resisting the pull of the weight stack rather than letting it snap the arm upward.\", \"concentric\": \"Pull the handle downward and slightly backward by driving the elbow down past the ribcage toward the hip on the working side, leading with scapular depression and retraction before the elbow flexes further. The torso remains stationary and square; only the arm and scapula move.\", \"tempo_notes\": \"Maintain continuous tension by not allowing the weight stack to touch down between repetitions; avoid using a rapid backward trunk lean to generate momentum at the start of the concentric phase.\", \"end_position\": \"Elbow at or just behind the plane of the torso, handle near the lower ribs or hip crease on the working side, with the scapula fully depressed and retracted.\", \"safety_notes\": [\"Ensure the thigh pad is snug enough to prevent the body from rising off the seat when pulling heavier loads.\", \"Avoid forcing the shoulder into extreme horizontal abduction at the top position if it produces anterior shoulder discomfort.\"], \"external_cues\": \"Pull the handle toward your hip pocket on the working side; keep the opposite shoulder pointed straight ahead at the pulley.\", \"internal_cues\": \"Drive the elbow down toward the hip before bending it further; keep the ribcage stacked over the pelvis and resist twisting toward the pulley.\", \"common_mistakes\": [\"Rotating the trunk toward the working arm to add apparent range of motion.\", \"Leaning backward excessively and using body momentum instead of scapular depression to initiate the pull.\", \"Flexing the elbow first instead of leading with the elbow driving down and back.\", \"Allowing the shoulder to shrug upward at the top of the eccentric phase instead of controlling scapular elevation.\", \"Using the non-working hand to pull the body sideways toward the pulley for extra range.\"], \"equipment_setup\": \"Attach a single D-handle (neutral/vertical grip) to a high pulley. The working arm is extended overhead with the handle at end range, scapula elevated and slightly protracted; the non-working hand rests on the thigh or grips the seat frame for stabilization.\", \"technical_failure\": \"The point at which completing the pull requires rotating the trunk toward the working side, leaning the torso backward beyond the established starting angle, or using the free hand to pull the body toward the pulley to manufacture range of motion.\", \"primary_joint_actions\": \"Glenohumeral extension and adduction with the elbow moving from an overhead position down toward the hip; elbow flexion is largely fixed isometrically at the handle rather than actively driven; scapula depresses and retracts on the working side; the trunk resists rotation and lateral flexion toward the loaded side.\"}" |172|EZ-Bar Curl                              |"{\"grip\": \"Grip the angled inner cambers of the bar with a semi-supinated orientation, hands roughly shoulder-width apart; the exact hand placement follows the bar's contour rather than a fixed measurement.\", \"tldr\": {\"focus\": \"Keep the elbows stationary at the ribcage and drive the motion purely through elbow flexion.\", \"setup\": \"Stand upright gripping the EZ-bar on the angled inner cambers, hands about shoulder-width apart, arms fully extended in front of the thighs.\", \"execution\": \"Flex the elbows to curl the bar upward in a fixed arc while the upper arms stay pinned to the torso.\", \"stop_when\": \"The elbows begin drifting forward or the torso starts swinging to sling the bar upward.\"}, \"stance\": \"Feet shoulder-width or slightly narrower, knees softly unlocked, weight balanced evenly.\", \"bracing\": \"Brace the abdominals and glutes to keep the pelvis and ribcage stacked, preventing lumbar hyperextension or hip-driven momentum as the bar rises.\", \"overview\": \"This is a standing biceps curl performed with a cambered EZ-bar, gripped on the angled sections so the wrists sit in a semi-supinated, semi-pronated position rather than the full supination of a straight bar. The camber reduces wrist and forearm torque while still placing the biceps brachii and brachialis under a comparable tension profile to a standard curl. This variant is distinct from a reverse-grip or wide pronated EZ-bar curl, both of which shift emphasis toward the brachioradialis and wrist extensors.\", \"eccentric\": \"Lower the bar back along the same arc under control by extending the elbows, resisting the load rather than letting it drop, until the arms are fully straight again.\", \"concentric\": \"Flex the elbows to lift the bar in an arc from the thighs toward the lower chest, keeping the upper arms fixed against the torso and allowing only the forearms to travel.\", \"tempo_notes\": \"Avoid using a bouncing rebound out of the bottom position; maintain continuous tension by not fully relaxing the elbows or resting the bar against the thighs between repetitions.\", \"end_position\": \"Elbows near-fully flexed with the bar approaching chest or lower-sternum height, upper arms still vertical.\", \"safety_notes\": [\"Avoid hyperextending the elbows aggressively at the bottom position under load.\", \"Keep the lower back neutral rather than arching to assist the lift.\"], \"external_cues\": \"Move the bar in a straight arc toward the collarbone; avoid letting the bar swing away from the body.\", \"internal_cues\": \"Keep the upper arms glued to the ribs; think of curling the forearm toward the shoulder rather than lifting the bar with the shoulders.\", \"common_mistakes\": [\"Swinging the torso backward and forward to generate momentum for the bar.\", \"Letting the elbows travel forward away from the ribcage as the set progresses.\", \"Using shoulder flexion to help lift the bar in the upper portion of the movement.\", \"Fully relaxing the elbows and resting the bar against the thighs between repetitions.\", \"Shrugging the shoulders upward as fatigue increases.\"], \"equipment_setup\": \"Use an EZ-curl bar loaded symmetrically; no bench or pad is required.\", \"range_of_motion\": \"From full elbow extension at the bottom (without hyperextending or relaxing biceps tension) to near-maximal elbow flexion at the top, limited by forearm-to-upper-arm contact.\", \"rir_0_definition\": \"Inability to complete the concentric arc through the full intended ROM using elbow flexion alone, even after allowing minor but still-controlled elbow drift.\", \"rir_1_indicators\": \"Bar speed slows noticeably in the mid-to-upper range, slight forward elbow drift appears but is quickly correctable, and full ROM is still achieved without torso assistance.\", \"individualization\": \"Hand spacing on the EZ-bar's angled sections may shift slightly based on forearm length and wrist comfort, and torso lean may vary marginally with limb proportions, provided the upper arms remain fixed against the torso and the bar path stays a consistent vertical arc.\", \"plane_of_movement\": \"Primarily sagittal-plane elbow flexion/extension, with the bar traveling in a fixed arc in front of the body and negligible movement in other planes.\", \"starting_position\": \"Stand with the torso upright, shoulders back and down, upper arms hanging vertically alongside the ribcage, elbows fully extended, and the bar resting against the thighs.\", \"technical_failure\": \"The point at which the elbows can no longer stay fixed against the torso and begin driving forward, or the torso initiates backward lean and rebound to continue moving the bar.\", \"primary_joint_actions\": \"Elbow flexion as the sole intended joint action; the shoulder remains in a stabilized, near-neutral extension position, and the wrist stays in a fixed semi-supinated angle throughout rather than actively moving.\"}" |136|Barbell Forward Lunge                    |"{\"grip\": \"Hands grip the bar just outside shoulder width, elbows pointing down and back to lift the chest and keep the bar secured against the back.\", \"tldr\": {\"focus\": \"Keep the torso upright and drive through the front heel to return to the start position rather than falling forward.\", \"setup\": \"Barbell rests across the upper back in a low-bar or high-bar squat position with feet together at the starting point.\", \"execution\": \"Step forward into a lunge, lower the rear knee toward the floor, then push back off the front foot to return to the starting stance before alternating legs.\", \"stop_when\": \"The front knee cannot maintain forward tracking and drifts inward, or the torso pitches forward to complete the return step.\"}, \"stance\": \"Feet begin together at hip width; the stepping leg advances forward into a split stance with the front shin roughly vertical at the bottom and the rear heel elevated.\", \"bracing\": \"Abdominal brace maintained throughout the step to prevent lumbar extension as the trunk decelerates the forward step; pelvis kept level to avoid lateral tilt during single-leg support.\", \"overview\": \"This is the alternating barbell forward lunge: the lifter steps forward from a static stance, lowers into a lunge, and then pushes back to the original standing position before stepping forward with the opposite leg. This differs from the walking lunge, in which the lifter continues forward with each step and never returns to the starting point, and from the reverse lunge, in which the working leg steps backward instead of forward. The forward-stepping action increases eccentric demand on the front leg's quadriceps and adductors during deceleration compared to the reverse lunge variant.\", \"eccentric\": \"The working leg steps forward and the body lowers under control as the front knee flexes and the hip flexes slightly, while the rear knee lowers toward the floor without contacting it; the trunk decelerates the forward momentum of the step rather than being carried passively.\", \"concentric\": \"From the bottom lunge position, the front leg drives through the heel and midfoot, extending the hip and knee to push the body back to the starting standing position; the rear leg assists by extending at the hip and knee as it returns to meet the front foot.\", \"tempo_notes\": \"The forward step and descent should be controlled rather than allowed to free-fall; the push-back to standing can be performed with continuous effort but should not involve a bounce off the bottom position.\", \"end_position\": \"Standing upright with both feet together, hips and knees fully extended, torso vertical, before the opposite leg initiates the next forward step.\", \"safety_notes\": [\"Ensure enough clear floor space in front of the lifter for the full forward step before beginning.\", \"Avoid contacting the rear knee against the floor under load.\", \"Keep the bar secured against the upper back throughout the step to prevent lateral shifting.\"], \"external_cues\": \"Step forward and lower straight down; push the floor away to return to the starting spot.\", \"internal_cues\": \"Sit down into the front hip rather than falling forward; drive the front heel into the floor to stand back up.\", \"common_mistakes\": [\"Allowing the front knee to travel excessively past the toes while the torso falls forward.\", \"Letting the front knee drift medially during the push-back phase.\", \"Taking a step that is too short, resulting in the front knee absorbing most of the load with minimal hip involvement.\", \"Rounding the lumbar spine to counterbalance the forward step.\", \"Pushing off the rear leg rather than the front leg during the return to standing.\"], \"equipment_setup\": \"Barbell positioned across the trapezius (high-bar) or rear deltoids (low-bar) as in a back squat, loaded on a squat rack for un-racking; sufficient floor space is required in front of the lifter for the forward step.\", \"range_of_motion\": \"The rear knee descends until it is just above the floor and the front knee reaches approximately 90 degrees of flexion; depth is limited by hip and ankle mobility and by the requirement to keep the front knee tracking over the foot rather than collapsing inward.\", \"rir_0_definition\": \"Inability to complete the return to standing without significant forward trunk collapse, loss of front-knee alignment, or use of the rear leg to push the body upright instead of the front leg.\", \"rir_1_indicators\": \"The push-back to standing becomes noticeably slower and requires visible trunk lean to assist, though the front knee still tracks correctly and full depth is still reached.\", \"individualization\": \"Step length may vary with limb proportions and hip mobility, provided the front shin remains close to vertical at the bottom and the rear knee lowers without striking the floor. Bar position (high-bar versus low-bar) may be adjusted for shoulder and thoracic mobility without altering the fundamental movement pattern.\", \"plane_of_movement\": \"Primarily sagittal-plane hip and knee flexion/extension, with a smaller frontal-plane stabilization component at the hip and ankle to control the forward step and return.\", \"starting_position\": \"Standing upright with feet together or hip-width apart, barbell secured across the upper back, ribcage stacked over the pelvis, knees soft but not locked.\", \"technical_failure\": \"The front knee valgus collapses inward, the torso pitches forward substantially to generate momentum for the return step, or the lifter can no longer control the forward step and instead falls into the bottom position.\", \"primary_joint_actions\": \"Front leg: hip flexion transitioning to hip extension, knee flexion transitioning to knee extension, ankle dorsiflexion under load. Rear leg: hip extension with knee flexion during the descent, then hip and knee extension to assist the push-back. Spine and pelvis are held in a stabilized, near-neutral position throughout.\"}"
